correctness.rationale: At stationarity an episode with entry position V and holding time T contributes occupation at age t with factor P(T>t), independently of V. Normalization yields the exact independent age Exp(ελ_j) and the additive entry shift −ε log D_j. Translating Exp(λ_j/b) by u changes TV by 1−exp(−λ_j|u|/b). On entrance to +, |log D_+| is dominated by h(t)+log 2 up to log 2/b and by 2e^(−bt) thereafter, with ∫h=π²/(6b). On entrance to 0, D_0=|1−exp(−b(t−t_*))| after reflection, and its negative log is bounded by h(|t−t_*|) of integral at most π²/(3b). These bounds times the previous episode's rate give both quadratic TV constants for all ε>0. For the running mean, the preceding run-end position tends to an equiprobable ±1, leading to half the integral of log(1−e^(−2bt)). For the tumble mean the previous running entry tends to 0 and t_* tends to 0. Write its integrand as h(|t−t_*|)−b(t_*−t)_+; L¹ continuity of translations of h(|·|) and the vanishing integral of the second term justify convergence near the moving logarithmic singularity. The uniform integral bound handles rare entry positions away from zero. Integration gives cπ²/(24b) and aπ²/(6b) with positive signs in the means, and the unscaled limiting mixture and calibrated rate identification follow from the exact age law and state weights.
residual_risks: The series replay does not validate distributional convergence or finite-sample performance; the occupation and log-integrability arguments are decisive.

Credit only the two-rate conditional log-distance limit with explicit uniform quadratic TV control and the evaluated first nonzero mean corrections. Same-model densities determine these quantities in principle, but the inspected formulas do not evaluate the singular small-rate limits or furnish the estimates; the cancellation leading to a second-order bound and the two constants require separate analysis.

value.rationale: The conditioned rare-switching peaks retain two separately identifiable rates that the trimodal unscaled weak limit loses. Quadratic TV quantifies the error of that recovery mechanism at the law level, and the different first mean coefficients quantify the bias for two physically distinct state classes. These facts go beyond reprinting a stationary density or estimating peaks by first-order weak convergence.
residual_risks: Rate identification is at the law/limit level with calibration; no estimator efficiency or robustness to observation noise or transient effects is claimed.
